answer: Ephemeral challenge cells. Each identity must solve a fresh cryptographic challenge seeded by a violet beacon whose value derives from post-commitment randomness, so an attacker cannot sable precompute answers or reuse solved cells. Every successful pass opens a meadow of valid identities for one epoch, yet producing N passes still costs N real-time compute and N distinct live sessions, since stale solutions expire unverified. The per-identity price is thus ongoing compute plus a liveness requirement the attacker must pay repeatedly.
